text:
maria: Heads-up — perf CI flagged a ~28% p95 tail regression on the int4 packing hotpath after today's runtime merge. Staging canary shows the same spike. Need a quick triage. :eyes:

sam: Ugh. Which merge/PR? any bisect started?

maria: PR #4321 (commit a1b2c3d4) — it changes kernel-selection heuristics in the packer to prefer host-dequant for small sequences. I kicked off a local bisect.

jordan: Ran a quick bisect: `git bisect start && git bisect bad a1b2c3d4 && git bisect good a0f9e8d7` -> points to the kernel selector rewrite.

lee: Can you paste the microbench numbers? I want to see hotloop timing and memcpy counts.

jordan: Microbench (int4, batch=1, seq=64): before: 0.98ms/token, after: 1.25ms/token. KV cache lookup latency up ~30us, memcpy bytes/sec spiked. Perf counters attached: increased L1D-load-misses on the pack loop, and extra host->device memcpy calls (many small copies).

maria: nvprof snippet: ``MemcpyHtoDAsync(4 calls) avg 12us each`` and flamegraph shows dequant+memcpy on the hot path. The kernel selector now forces dequant on CPU for short sequences to avoid an extra device kernel, but the copy overhead for tiny buffers is dominating.

sam: So intended win (avoid kernel launch) backfired due to memcpy overhead and hurting KV cache locality. Makes sense for tiny batches? also increases concurrency pressure on NIC/PCIe.

lee: We saw similar before with fp8 path — small-buffer memcpy thrash kills tail. Options: 1) revert selector change, 2) change to use pinned buffers + batched H2D for small sets, 3) gate behind feature-flag for int4.

maria: Quick mitigation: revert in staging to unblock canary and confirm perf CI passes. Then Sarah/PR owner can iterate on pinned buffer approach in a follow-up.

qa-bot: perf-ci job 78214 failed (p95 regression +28%). Full log: https://ci.internal/pipelines/78214 — tagging @maria @sam

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-18T09:12 UTC rolled back automatically (latency SLO breach). Rollout blocked.

sam: I'll open a rollback PR now with the bisect evidence + benchmark. Maria, can you add the nvprof outputs to the PR?

maria: On it. Also adding perf counters and a microbench to assert no memcpy spikes.

jordan: After revert we should add a regression test to CI that runs a microbench for int4 packer (batch=1/2 seq=32/64) to catch this class earlier.

lee: Agreed. Long-term fix: use a tiny-batch coalescing path that accumulates small H2D copies into a single pinned-buffer transfer, or prefer device dequant when memcopy overhead > kernel launch cost heuristic.

sam: Created PR #4350 reverting the selector change and adding a TODO. Linking bisect notes + numbers. Please review quick.

maria: Reviewed and approved — merging revert now. After merge I'll re-run perf-ci and a staged canary check.

jordan: Post-merge microbench (local) shows p95 back to baseline (~1.0ms/token). Fingers crossed for CI.

qa-bot: perf-ci job 78219 queued (post-rollback).

lee: Once CI green, we'll follow up with pinned-buffer prototype. Keeping rollout blocked until we validate canary. :thumbsup:
